query: What drives customer satisfaction (Overall Rating) across the different airlines?

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: A qualitative service-handling dimension (responsive/proactive vs. dismissive/unresolved) plausibly extracted from the review text. It lies outside the Overall Rating focus, is not a deterministic function of it, and is not knowable only after the outcome (it describes an in-service experience). Service responsiveness is a well-known driver of airline satisfaction, so it plausibly carries predictive signal. It also captures complaint-resolution / responsiveness nuance not fully encoded by the existing numeric 'Staff Service' rating, so it can add incremental leverage.

per_column.name: value_perception
per_column.rationale: Perceived price fairness / value for money is a distinct construct from the overall satisfaction score (not a restatement, component, or deterministic function of Overall Rating), and it is strongly correlated with satisfaction, so it is a legitimate predictor of the focus. The caveat is that it is essentially a re-expression of the ALREADY-PRESENT 'Value For Money' original column; relative to the focus it is a predictor, but it adds little NEW predictive information beyond what the model already has, so its incremental utility is low.

judge.rationale: Both added columns are genuine predictors of Overall Rating rather than restatements or leakage of the focus itself: each is a separate experiential/perceptual dimension that plausibly drives satisfaction and is knowable at review time. However, incremental predictive leverage beyond the original columns is only moderate. 'customer_service_responsiveness' contributes the most new signal, since it encodes qualitative service-handling detail not fully captured by the numeric 'Staff Service' field. 'value_perception' is a legitimate driver but largely duplicates the existing 'Value For Money' column, which is one of the strongest predictors already available, so it adds little that a model doesn't already have. Net: a valid but partially redundant predictor set, hence moderate-to-low set-level utility.
